A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Spec-o3 work. Their complete main texts and appendices support comparison, with readable tables, equations and figures. Retained material can be matched despite appendix renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark and generalization experiments, training/tool ablations, and human evaluations of reasoning quality.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds original QSO, low-SNR, data-efficiency, synthetic-trajectory and throughput results.

M1.justification: The core architecture, inspection loop, SFT/GRPO objectives and reward remain unchanged. Appendices H/J add an auxiliary QSO adaptation procedure using few-shot, answer-guided GPT-5.2 trajectories, Gemini filtering and expert acceptance, followed by incremental SFT.

E1.justification: V2 adds high-redshift QSO evaluation and adaptation, plus CV verification under simulated severe noise (SNR below 5). These extend coverage to substantially different spectral morphology and degraded input conditions. The original LAMOST, SDSS/DESI and O/B/A coverage remains.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds the science-specialized S1-VL-32B and its cold-start-fine-tuned S1-VL-32B-SFT variant. All previously evaluated comparators remain; these additions do not extend to the retained cross-survey and cross-task tables.

E3.justification: New protocols include QSO and low-SNR tests with 50 positives and 250 negatives, Gaussian-noise injection into CV positives, approximately 200 SFT trajectories followed by full-data RL, and incremental SFT on 96 synthetic QSO trajectories. V2 also introduces a throughput assessment. Existing benchmark splits, metrics and core training settings are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained training-stage and tool-access ablations, v2 tests cold-start data reduction, three trajectory-generation conditions, and lightweight QSO adaptation. The new QSO and low-SNR evaluations also probe generalization and robustness boundaries absent from v1.

E5.justification: The human/LLM score distributions and Spearman-correlation reporting are unchanged. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, random-seed reporting, confidence intervals or significance tests. Its new trajectory acceptance counts are additional outcomes rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Retained entries in Tables 1–4 are unchanged. New results include S1-VL comparisons, QSO zero-shot F1 of 71.9 and low-SNR F1 of 78.2 for Spec-o3-7B, and 3B QSO F1 of 73.6 after adaptation versus 68.4 zero-shot. Tables 12–13 add data-efficiency and synthesis outcomes; Section 4.7 reports approximately 0.2 seconds per spectrum in throughput.

T1.justification: The state and trajectory definitions, reward equation, and rollout algorithm are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and v2's expanded behavioral explanations introduce no new formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion add a quantified practical claim: approximately 50-fold throughput over manual inspection on an eight-H100 server. The central accuracy, cross-survey/task generalization and explanation-quality claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix G replaces the simple declining-tool-use account with explanations involving nonmonotonic exploration and evidence-dependent stopping, using unchanged Figure 6. V2 also interprets annotation efficiency and noise robustness, distinguishes bulk throughput from single-sample processing, and explains specialist DL screening as complementary to Spec-o3 vetting. The formal limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 documents the GPT-5.2 generator, Gemini-2.5-Pro filter, seed examples and expert acceptance used for synthetic data. It adds inference hardware and asynchronous tool-execution information and revises LAMOST instrument specifications. Existing core training disclosures and the project access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for S1-VL, post-training/distillation work and inference engines. Section 2.3 shifts its distinction from generic image agents toward scientific knowledge alignment, while Appendix F clarifies complementary screening/vetting roles. Publication-year and venue updates for retained references do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: V2 edits the abstract and contribution bullets, expands the training-dynamics discussion, and adds an efficiency subsection, acknowledgements and supporting appendices. Most existing prose and the main narrative order remain. Affiliation, contact and bibliographic text also receive limited edits.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains two rows, and six compact appendix tables are added. All seven figures retain their content and design. Existing displays are redistributed, including the human rubric moving from Table 7 to Table 11 and the unchanged rollout algorithm moving to a later page.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for practical extensibility. V1 left annotation burden untested; Table 12 now shows CV/CS performance within three F1 points using roughly one-fifth the demonstrations, while Table 9 demonstrates adaptation using 96 synthetic QSO trajectories. New science-specialized comparisons and QSO/noise tests strengthen the empirical case further. The throughput protocol remains sparsely specified and uncertainty reporting is unchanged, but the added controlled experiments address important gaps in the scalability argument.
